title: ISic001037. Fragment of a monumental Greek inscription
body:
Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa, Jonathan Prag
1[--- β]ασιλ[εὺς? ---]

Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa, Jonathan Prag
1[---.]ΑΣΙΛ[...---]

Facsimile Images

Apparatus criticus

  • Text after Schubring (who proposes [Β]ασιλ[έως])

translation

commentary

Although the various texts reported from the 'grotta dei cavalli' seemingly referencing Hieron as king are generally considered as early modern forgeries (strongly argued by Pugliese Carratelli, who notes that the location is itself only quarried out in the Byzantine period), there has never been any suggestion that this piece should be questioned; it has however been very largely ignored. It is notably similar to ISic002747 fragment b, but given that the latter is one of four fragments excavated by Orsi from Castello Eurialo in 1904, it seems impossible that it can be the same. That fact would therefore seem rather to speak in its favour, namely the existence of other similar monumental texts, besides those of the Syracusan theatre itself, which was the parallel that Schubring noted. The implication of the fragment is that of monumental construction supported by Hieron II.

bibliography

  • Schubring 1861-1867 669 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10001601
  • Kaibel 1890 216 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10001072
  • Pugliese Carratelli 1956 no.57 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10001394

Described by Schurbing as fine ('schoenen') letters, in the same script as those of the theatre at Syracuse.
